subject: US Q1 regime under cross-asset divergence
claim: Within Q1-labeled periods, simultaneous cross-asset divergence and aligned systematic cutting are associated with weaker 10-day broad-equity outcomes than Q1 periods without that conjunction.
hypothesis: Within Q1-labeled periods, simultaneous cross-asset divergence and aligned systematic cutting are associated with weaker 10-day broad-equity outcomes than Q1 periods without that conjunction.
falsifier: Falsified if, after at least 25 independent events, the mean 10-day SPY excess outcome under the conjunction is not at least 1 percentage point below the Q1 no-conjunction baseline.

subject: Q2 cross-asset divergence
claim: When an equity Q2 regime is simultaneously contradicted by both FX-dollar and rates-credit legs, subsequent 21-day equity-regime persistence is lower than for Q2 observations without that dual contradiction.
hypothesis: When an equity Q2 regime is simultaneously contradicted by both FX-dollar and rates-credit legs, subsequent 21-day equity-regime persistence is lower than for Q2 observations without that dual contradiction.
falsifier: Reject if, after at least 30 independent Q2 observations, dual-contradiction cases do not reduce 21-day Q2 persistence by at least 10 percentage points versus other Q2 observations.

subject: Fed net-liquidity acceleration and breadth
claim: In low-volatility regimes, negative 10-day acceleration in Fed net liquidity is associated with 21-day breadth deterioration after controlling for starting breadth and the growth-inflation regime.
hypothesis: In low-volatility regimes, negative 10-day acceleration in Fed net liquidity is associated with 21-day breadth deterioration after controlling for starting breadth and the growth-inflation regime.
falsifier: Reject if the matched low-volatility sample produces AUC below 0.55, if starting breadth alone reproduces the association, or if sign-shuffled liquidity acceleration performs comparably to the observed series.

subject: US regime-label transition
claim: When the confirmed US macro quad remains unsupported by its raw axes for at least four sessions while liquidity is contracting, near-term board claims may show weaker signed excess than claims made after label and axes realign.
hypothesis: When the confirmed US macro quad remains unsupported by its raw axes for at least four sessions while liquidity is contracting, near-term board claims may show weaker signed excess than claims made after label and axes realign.
falsifier: Falsified if, after at least 30 eligible observations, five-day signed excess during unsupported-label/contracting-liquidity states is not at least 0.5 percentage point lower than during aligned-label states.

subject: US regime transition and credit divergence
claim: When the confirmed US regime label remains Q2 while raw axes indicate Q3 for at least five sessions, and credit is the dominant rising risk-radar scare despite a risk-on tape, subsequent 21-session US-equity excess returns are weaker than in otherwise comparable Q2 observations without that joint disagreement.
hypothesis: When the confirmed US regime label remains Q2 while raw axes indicate Q3 for at least five sessions, and credit is the dominant rising risk-radar scare despite a risk-on tape, subsequent 21-session US-equity excess returns are weaker than in otherwise comparable Q2 observations without that joint disagreement.
falsifier: Reject if, after at least 30 independent observations, the mean 21-session signed SPY excess return under the joint disagreement is not at least 2 percentage points below the matched Q2-without-disagreement cohort.

subject: Credit-versus-tape divergence
claim: When a risk-on tape with broad participation coexists with a rising credit-dominant radar, deterioration should appear first in credit-sensitive relative performance rather than as an immediate index-level drawdown.
hypothesis: When a risk-on tape with broad participation coexists with a rising credit-dominant radar, deterioration should appear first in credit-sensitive relative performance rather than as an immediate index-level drawdown.
falsifier: Falsified if, across at least 20 comparable observations, credit-sensitive relative performance does not weaken before index drawdowns or the median lead is zero or negative.

subject: US regime-transition entry quality
claim: When the confirmed US regime label remains Q2 while its own axes indicate pending Q3 and liquidity is contracting, existing US-board long entries may exhibit weaker 21-day signed excess than matched Q2 entries without that divergence.
hypothesis: When the confirmed US regime label remains Q2 while its own axes indicate pending Q3 and liquidity is contracting, existing US-board long entries may exhibit weaker 21-day signed excess than matched Q2 entries without that divergence.
falsifier: Reject if, after at least 30 matched observations, mean 21-day signed excess during label/axis divergence is not at least 2 percentage points below the matched non-divergent Q2 cohort.
